doc: Mission 5, DART (September 26, 2022): 'Push an asteroid' (issue #49). The crew fly it from mission control. (1) Find Dimorphos: through DRACO, DART's camera (a 0.29-degree view, about 0.5 arcsec per pixel, S-dart-nssdc), Didymos (780 m) is one dot; as DART closes in at about 6.58 km/s (S-dart-nssdc) the dot splits in two and the player locks on the small moon, Dimorphos (160 m, S-dart-nasa), as DART's SMARTNav did in the last 4 hours (S-dart-nssdc). (2) Steer: small thruster pulses keep Dimorphos in the crosshair; the miss at impact follows from the sideways speed left; past Dimorphos's edge: lost, tried again. (3) The last picture: the player takes it as late as possible; its sharpness follows from the distance and DRACO's 0.5 arcsec pixel (the real last images, about 2 s before impact, were about 3 cm per pixel, S-dart-nssdc). Time runs fast through the last hours (said on screen: 1,500, 300, then 6 times), real time for the last 20 s; drift alarms now and then (our simplification) make the player correct the aim fast. (4) Weeks later: telescopes watch the pair's light dip each time Dimorphos passes Didymos; the light scrolls by, 3 hours each second (said on screen), and the player taps SPACE on each deep dip, before the impact and after; Dimorphos's orbit went from 11 h 55 min to 11 h 23 min, 32 minutes shorter, plus or minus about 2 (S-dart-nasa-period). Our simplifications, said here: the distance between the two asteroids (no figure found on a NASA page; ours: 1.2 km), the drift of the aim, the thruster pulses (each moves the hit about 6 m) and their number, the light curve's shape and noise, the shapes of the asteroids.

texts.find: Through DRACO, DART's camera. Watch the dot: when it splits in two, pick the small moon (A/D) and lock it (Enter).
texts.fast: Four hours from impact: shown 1,500 times faster.
texts.steer: Keep the hit on Dimorphos: WASD fires thrusters. Alarms: the aim drifts, correct it fast!
texts.photo: Take the last picture (SPACE) as late as you dare: the closer, the sharper. After the impact there is no signal.
texts.measure: Weeks later, telescopes watch the pair's light (3 hours each second): SPACE when each deep dip crosses the line.
texts.big_sub: That is not how it went: DART's SMARTNav switched to the small moon, Dimorphos. Try again.
texts.miss_sub: That is not how it went: DART hit Dimorphos almost dead center. Try again.
texts.few_sub: The team needed a clear measurement. Try again.

facts.text: On September 26, 2022, DART hit Dimorphos on purpose. Its last images, about 2 seconds before impact, were about 3 cm per pixel.
NASA confirmed the impact shortened Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes: 32 minutes, plus or minus about 2.
